The invention relates to an organic thin film transistor capable of achieving high charge mobility and improved transistor performance.

The organic thin film transistor includes a base material, a gate electrode provided on the base material, a gate insulating layer formed over the gate electrode, an organic semiconductor layer, and source and drain electrodes electrically connected to the organic semiconductor layer. The transistor is configured so that charge can be efficiently injected from the source and drain electrodes into the organic semiconductor layer, thereby enhancing carrier transport and enabling high mobility operation.

In this transistor, charge injection layers are provided between the source electrode and the layer located beneath the source electrode on the base material side, and also between the drain electrode and the layer located beneath the drain electrode on the base material side. These charge injection layers facilitate the injection of charges between the electrodes and the organic semiconductor layer or adjacent underlying layers, reducing contact resistance and improving device characteristics.

Each charge injection layer is formed so that its thickness gradually decreases in a direction away from the facing direction between the source electrode and the drain electrode. In other words, the charge injection layer is thicker near the region where the source and drain electrodes face each other and becomes thinner toward the outer side of each electrode. This thickness profile contributes to more effective charge injection in the channel region and supports high mobility in the organic thin film transistor.

The invention also provides a method for manufacturing the organic thin film transistor. In this method, a metal layer is first formed and then irradiated and scanned with a laser to pattern the metal layer, thereby forming the source electrode and the drain electrode. Subsequently, a solution containing a material for forming the charge injection layers is added dropwise to selected regions. The solution spreads and dries to form charge injection layers having the desired tapered thickness profile. By using laser scanning and dropwise addition, the source and drain electrodes and the charge injection layers can be formed efficiently and accurately, making it possible to manufacture an organic thin film transistor with high mobility and improved reliability.
outputs.L4:
An organic thin film transistor and a method of manufacturing the same are provided. The organic thin film transistor includes a base material, a gate electrode formed on the base material, a gate insulating layer disposed over the gate electrode, an organic semiconductor layer formed on the gate insulating layer, and source and drain electrodes electrically connected to the organic semiconductor layer. Charge injection layers are provided between the source and drain electrodes and the organic semiconductor layer, or between the source and drain electrodes and underlying conductive or semiconductor layers, in order to facilitate efficient charge transfer.

The charge injection layers have a tapered shape. This tapered structure reduces abrupt interface discontinuities and improves electrical contact between the electrodes and the organic semiconductor layer. As a result, contact resistance is reduced and charge carriers can be injected more smoothly from the source electrode into the organic semiconductor layer and extracted more efficiently through the drain electrode.

The charge injection layers may be formed by first providing a metal layer on selected portions of the transistor structure. A laser is then scanned over the metal layer to modify, pattern, or activate predetermined regions of the metal layer. After the laser-scanning step, a charge-injection-layer solution is added dropwise to the scanned portions. The solution preferentially wets or reacts with the laser-treated regions, thereby forming tapered charge injection layers at the desired positions. The taper may be controlled by adjusting laser-scanning conditions, the composition and viscosity of the charge-injection-layer solution, the amount of solution dispensed, and drying or curing conditions.

Because the charge injection layers are formed only in selected regions, the manufacturing process can be simplified and material waste can be reduced. The laser-scanning process also enables precise local treatment without requiring complex photolithographic patterning. Accordingly, the method is suitable for manufacturing organic thin film transistors on various substrates, including flexible base materials.

By introducing the tapered charge injection layers between the electrodes and the underlying layers, the organic thin film transistor exhibits improved charge injection characteristics, reduced contact resistance, and enhanced carrier mobility. These improvements contribute to better switching behavior, higher current output, and improved overall transistor performance. The device and manufacturing method are therefore useful for organic electronic devices such as flexible displays, sensors, radio-frequency identification tags, and other printed or solution-processed electronic systems.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest and most common words in the English language, yet it plays an important role in communication. It is called the definite article, and it helps us speak about something specific. For example, when we say “a book,” we may mean any book. But when we say “the book,” we are talking about a particular book that the listener or reader can identify.

This simple word gives clarity and direction to a sentence. It helps connect ideas and points to people, places, objects, or events that are already known or important in context. Phrases like “the sun,” “the world,” and “the future” feel familiar because “the” makes them sound unique and significant.

Although it is easy to overlook, “the” is essential in English. It shapes meaning, adds precision, and makes language smoother. Without it, many sentences would sound incomplete or unclear. In this way, “the” proves that even the smallest words can have great importance.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for an organic thin film transistor that improves mobility using tapered charge injection layers formed near source and drain electrodes after laser scanning a metal layer.
counterfactuals.output: An organic thin film transistor includes a substrate, a gate electrode, a gate insulating layer, source and drain electrodes, an organic semiconductor layer, and charge injection layers disposed adjacent to the source and drain electrodes. The charge injection layers are formed by providing a metal layer in contact with or proximate to the source and drain electrodes and irradiating the metal layer with a laser beam to locally modify, diffuse, oxidize, or redistribute the metal material. The laser scanning forms tapered charge injection regions extending from the source and drain electrodes toward a channel region, each tapered region having a thickness or concentration that gradually decreases with distance from the corresponding electrode. The tapered charge injection layers reduce carrier injection barriers and contact resistance between the electrodes and the organic semiconductor layer while suppressing abrupt field concentration at electrode edges. As a result, charge carriers are efficiently injected into the organic semiconductor layer, thereby improving field-effect mobility, current on/off characteristics, and operational stability of the organic thin film transistor.

【課題】  
有機半導体層とソース電極およびドレイン電極との界面における電荷注入障壁を低減し、低電圧駆動、高移動度、低接触抵抗および優れた動作安定性を実現可能な有機薄膜トランジスタを提供する。

【解決手段】  
基材上に、ゲート電極と、該ゲート電極を被覆するゲート絶縁層と、該ゲート絶縁層上に形成された有機半導体層と、該有機半導体層に電気的に接続されたソース電極およびドレイン電極とを備える有機薄膜トランジスタにおいて、前記有機半導体層と前記ソース電極および／またはドレイン電極との間に、電荷注入層を設ける。前記電荷注入層は、有機半導体層へのキャリア注入を促進する材料からなり、電極と有機半導体層とのエネルギー準位整合を改善することにより、接触抵抗を低減し、オン電流を向上させる。これにより、簡易な素子構成でありながら、良好なトランジスタ特性および高い信頼性を有する有機薄膜トランジスタを得ることができる。

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft an abstract for a patent application on a method of manufacturing an organic thin film transistor with charge injection layers between each source/drain electrode and the underlying base-side layer, where the layer thickness decreases away from the opposing electrode side.
counterfactuals.output: A method of manufacturing an organic thin film transistor includes forming a gate electrode, a gate insulating layer, and a base-side layer including an organic semiconductor layer, and forming source and drain electrodes over the base-side layer with respective charge injection layers interposed between the source and drain electrodes and the base-side layer. Each charge injection layer is formed so as to have a thickness profile that decreases in a direction away from a side of the corresponding electrode facing the opposing electrode, thereby providing a relatively thick charge injection region adjacent a channel region and a relatively thin region toward an outer side of the electrode. The thickness profile may be formed by controlled deposition through a mask, oblique deposition, surface-energy patterning, etch-back processing, or selective material removal. The resulting graded charge injection layers reduce contact resistance and improve carrier injection from the source and drain electrodes into the organic semiconductor while suppressing parasitic leakage and maintaining device stability.
